autofarm.title: AutoFarm Control Panel
autofarm.status.harvest.done: Harvest: last crop taken and replanted
autofarm.notice.mine_timeout: Harvest: can't break this one, skipped
autofarm.notice.no_seed: Harvest: out of seeds (none in the backpack either), replant skipped
autofarm.notice.seed_from_backpack: Harvest: moved seeds from backpack to hotbar
autofarm.notice.plant_no_seed: Plant: no seeds on hand - heading to the supply point
autofarm.notice.pick_failed: Harvest: couldn't pick this bush (right-click did nothing)
autofarm.notice.out_of_seeds: Out of seeds - heading to the supply point after this route
autofarm.notice.paused_low_health: Safety: health too low, paused (resumes when healed)
autofarm.notice.inventory_full_no_supply: Inventory full with no usable storage block: harvesting stopped
autofarm.notice.supply_unreachable: Supply: can't get to the supply point
autofarm.notice.supply_not_container: Supply: that block is not a storage block
autofarm.notice.supply_no_spot: Supply: nowhere to stand next to the supply point
autofarm.notice.supply_closed: Supply: the container screen got closed
autofarm.notice.supply_no_seed: Supply: no matching seeds in the container
autofarm.enabled.tip: Toggle it any time in game with the keybind (default `), no need to open this panel. Turning it off and on again clears the memory of already-visited targets, so crops that are still standing get recognised again - press it twice when it gets stuck.
autofarm.scan_interval.tip: How often the area is rescanned. Smaller is more responsive but costs more CPU. 20 ticks = 1s; with See-through on, the interval is automatically raised to at least 2s
autofarm.refill.tip: When replanting finds no seeds in your hotbar, it finishes the current route first, then makes one trip to the supply point. It takes items that plant into a crop block (i.e. seeds); if it knows which crop was missing, it only takes that one.
autofarm.deposit.tip: When free slots drop to 1 or fewer, it drops the current route and goes to store things. Which category gets stored, kept, or partly kept is decided per category in the Storage policy table (by default: seeds / food / blocks / tools are never stored, self-seeding crops like carrot, potato and sugar cane keep 1 stack, and raw produce like wheat is stored entirely). If the inventory fills up with no supply point configured (or that block is not storage), it stops harvesting instead of dropping crops.
autofarm.optimize.tip: Builds an initial route by always heading to the nearest target, then repeatedly reverses segments with 2-opt to shorten it. Turn off to keep the plain greedy order, which wanders noticeably more.
autofarm.show_path.tip: Draws the route as a line in the world so you can see exactly how it plans to walk.
autofarm.lock_sprint.tip: Keeps sprinting while travelling, nearly doubling movement speed (mining speed is unaffected). It only applies while the mod is driving your character and actually moving forward - it releases on arrival, while mining, and whenever you open a screen. Vanilla hunger limits still apply; the cost is a faster hunger drain.
autofarm.auto_eat.tip: When hunger drops to 6 or below (the point where vanilla stops letting you sprint), eats the hotbar food that restores the most hunger, then carries on walking. It stands still while eating, only touches your hotbar, and releases the key immediately if you open a screen or turn the option off.
autofarm.option.eat_full: Eat until the hunger bar is full
autofarm.eat_full.tip: Once it starts eating, it keeps going until the hunger bar is full instead of stopping the moment it can sprint again. Stopping early leaves hunger hovering around 7-8, so it would have to sit down for another bite every half minute or so. Eating to full stretches that gap several times over. If the food runs out mid-way it stops and gets back to work.
autofarm.allow_mine.tip: When going around is expensive, dig straight through the blocks in the way. Cost uses the vanilla formula for real break time, so mining stone with an iron pickaxe is cheap and punching obsidian bare-handed is avoided automatically. This changes your terrain, so it is off by default.
autofarm.allow_place.tip: Place blocks underfoot to cross ditches and climb ledges. It uses blocks from your hotbar, so put the material you want it to spend there. Off by default.
autofarm.auto_tool.tip: Before mining, swap to the most suitable tool in your hotbar (hotbar only, never digs into your inventory). It scores tools exactly like the vanilla break speed does, so the right tool is over three times faster. Keeps your hand as-is when nothing is better.
autofarm.through_walls.tip: Outlines ignore block occlusion, so you can see mature crops through walls, dirt and grass. It draws more, so scanning is throttled automatically
autofarm.display.hint: Draw outlines in the world so you can see what was scanned
autofarm.freecam_pause.tip: While a free camera / disembodied view is active, the mod stops driving your character and only keeps drawing outlines and routes. Watching a player stand perfectly still while blocks break themselves looks odd, hence the option. Outlines and routes are computed from the camera anyway, so you can also just fly around and watch it work with this left off.
autofarm.highlight.title: Outline Style
autofarm.highlight.preview.hint: Roughly how it looks in game
autofarm.supply.not_container: That block is not storage (chest / barrel / any storage mod works)
autofarm.default_seed.tip: Picks which hotbar slot is reserved for seeds (click to cycle 1-9). Two uses: replanting prefers that slot, and when fetching seeds from the container with no free slot left in your inventory, that seed stack is swapped straight into it (whatever was there goes back into the container), so seeds always have somewhere to land.
autofarm.storage.tip: When storing things: which category is kept in full, which is stored in full, and which keeps a few stacks - all set per category here. Defaults: seeds / food / blocks / tools are never stored, self-seeding crops like carrots and potatoes keep 1 stack, and harvest food like beetroot plus raw produce like wheat is stored entirely.
autofarm.storage.title: Storage Policy
autofarm.storage.hint.1: Left-click a row to cycle forward, right-click backward
autofarm.storage.hint.2: Order: Keep all -> Store all -> Keep 1~5 stacks
autofarm.storage.hint.3: Hover a row for the rule, vanilla examples,
autofarm.storage.hint.4: and what is in your inventory right now
autofarm.storage.current.none: In inventory: nothing of this kind
autofarm.category.seed.tip: Items that grow into a crop but cannot be eaten (true seeds). Kept by default - running out means a trip to the supply point.
autofarm.category.seed.examples: wheat seeds, beetroot seeds, pumpkin seeds, melon seeds, nether wart
autofarm.category.self_seed.tip: The harvest itself is what you replant: either edible as well, or it simply grows back into itself. Keeps 1 stack by default and stores the rest - storing all leaves nothing to plant, keeping all fills your inventory.
autofarm.category.self_seed.examples: carrot, potato, sugar cane, bamboo, cactus
autofarm.category.food.tip: Edible, cannot be planted, and not recognisable as the harvest of a crop. Kept by default - you need it when hunger stops you sprinting.
autofarm.category.food.examples: bread, steak, baked potato, golden apple
autofarm.category.harvest_food.tip: Edible, and clearly the harvest of a crop, yet it cannot be replanted: what you plant is a seed item and what you harvest is a different item. Beetroot is the classic case (beetroot seeds go in, beetroot comes out). Stored entirely by default - it is just food and only wastes slots.
autofarm.category.block.tip: Places a block, but that block is not a crop. Kept by default - it may be used to bridge gaps.
autofarm.category.block.examples: stone, dirt, planks (blocks that grow nothing)
autofarm.category.tool.tip: Anything with durability. Kept by default.
autofarm.category.tool.examples: pickaxe, axe, shovel, hoe, sword, bow
autofarm.category.produce.tip: Harvest that is neither food, nor a block, nor a durability item. Stored entirely by default - carrying it only wastes slots.
autofarm.category.produce.examples: wheat, sugar, most modded crop fruit that is neither food nor a block
autofarm.show_hud.tip: Keeps a small status readout in the top-left corner: what it is doing right now, how much it has harvested this round, how many replantable items you still carry, plus the reason whenever something is wrong (inventory full, out of seeds, safety pause). All of that used to be visible only inside the panel - and opening a screen is the last thing you want to do while harvesting.
autofarm.hud.title: AutoFarm - %s
autofarm.low_health.tip: Stops immediately when health drops below the chosen value, waits for you, and resumes on its own once healed - no need to flip the switch again. Default 4 hearts (half health). While harvesting your character keeps looking down, so a sneak attack or a fall is easy to miss; this is the seatbelt. Click to cycle: off -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 hearts.
autofarm.mobs_near.tip: Pauses when a hostile mob (zombie, skeleton, creeper, spider and the like) comes within 8 blocks. It only stops - it will not fight or run for you; the point is to never stand there harvesting while being hit.
autofarm.crop.summary: Filter: %s - Plant empty farmland: %s (%s spots nearby)
autofarm.fill_empty.tip: Besides the cell it just harvested, it also sows nearby farmland that has nothing growing on it. What gets planted is decided by the Crop filter screen (by default the seed type you carry the most of). It consumes seeds, so it is off by default.
autofarm.crop.tip: Choose which crops to harvest and which to leave alone, plus what to sow on empty farmland. Defaults to harvesting everything.
autofarm.crop.title: Crop Filter
autofarm.crop.mode.label: Filter mode: %s
autofarm.crop.mode.tip.off: Harvests every mature crop nearby and ignores the list entirely.
autofarm.crop.mode.tip.whitelist: Harvests only the checked crops and leaves the rest alone. Switching to this mode checks every crop found nearby first, so you uncheck what you do not want instead of starting from nothing.
autofarm.crop.mode.tip.blacklist: The checked crops are the ones it will NOT harvest; everything else is fair game. Handy when you only want to exclude one or two.
autofarm.crop.mode.tip.only_replantable: Ignores the list and asks your inventory instead: a crop you have no seeds for is left standing, because harvesting it only leaves bare farmland. It gets harvested once seeds come back from the supply point.
autofarm.crop.list.ignored: (this list is unused in the current mode)
autofarm.crop.list.empty: No crops found nearby - stand in your field and open this screen
autofarm.crop.tip.unchecked: Not on the list (left-click to add)
autofarm.crop.tip.seeds: Seeds of this type on hand: %s
autofarm.crop.fill_empty.tip: Sows farmland that has nothing growing on it. When off, only the cell it just harvested gets replanted.
autofarm.crop.plant.tip: Which crop gets sown on empty farmland. Click to cycle: auto -> wheat -> carrot -> ... The candidates are only the seed types you actually carry, so you can never pick something you cannot plant.
autofarm.crop.plant.hint.1: What goes on empty farmland: the crop chosen above,
autofarm.crop.plant.hint.2: or the seed type you carry most of when set to auto.
autofarm.extras.tip: Optional enhancements, all off by default: safety & stealth, anti-kick, behavior realism, tool upkeep, recovery & stats, dropped-item pickup, plus a separate high-risk combat group. Nothing changes unless you turn it on.
autofarm.extras.title: Extras
autofarm.extras.note: Apart from "Combat (high risk)", everything here only affects pacing and convenience and never bypasses game rules. The combat entry makes the mod attack mobs for you: it is high risk, off by default, and asks for confirmation before it turns on.
autofarm.danger.title: High-risk feature
autofarm.danger.subtitle: We do not recommend enabling Auto-attack
autofarm.danger.body1: "Auto-attack" is equivalent to the well-known "Kill Aura" and counts as cheating. Using it on multiplayer servers may be logged by anti-cheat, reported by other players, and lead to kicks, bans or rollbacks — the consequences are yours to bear.
autofarm.danger.body2: The default "non-violent" mode is built to look human: it turns to aim before striking and keeps random gaps between hits, so it is slower than a human hand. That only lowers the chance of being detected — it does not make you safe, and because it is slow your character can still be killed by mobs in a fight.
autofarm.danger.body3: Only enable it if you understand and accept these consequences. You can still turn it off from this panel at any time.
autofarm.antikick.tip: A whole set of "act more human" measures: turning is no longer uniform, aim no longer sits exactly on the block centre, footsteps occasionally falter, sprinting comes and goes, it hesitates before acting and "tires" over time. It never bypasses game rules, it just sands off the machine feel.
autofarm.antikick_level.tip: Light only scrambles timing. Medium adds aim tremor, stumbling steps, sprint gaps and a pause before acting. High adds a fatigue model, footstep offset and an occasional suboptimal route. Stronger looks more human and is slower. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.pause_player.tip: Stop harvesting when another player is nearby, and resume once they leave. Being seen by a player is the most common way auto-farming gets noticed.
autofarm.value_radius.tip: How close a player must be to trigger the pause. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.humanize.tip: Pause briefly at random after each crop before moving on, so the rhythm isn't metronome-perfect. Slightly slower.
autofarm.random_rest.tip: Take a short break automatically after working for a while, like a real player.
autofarm.rest_interval.tip: How long to work before each break. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.rest_duration.tip: How long each break lasts. Only used when scheduled rests are on.
autofarm.replace_tool.tip: When the held tool is nearly broken, swap in a same-kind tool with more durability from your inventory. Does nothing if none is better.
autofarm.durability.tip: Swap when remaining durability drops below this percentage. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.failure_cooldown.tip: When a crop can't be harvested, skip it for a short cooldown and retry automatically, instead of dropping it for the whole run.
autofarm.cooldown.tip: How long before a failed target is retried. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.verbose_hud.tip: Show one more line on the status HUD: elapsed working time and replanted count.
autofarm.pickup_drops.tip: Sweep up crop drops left lying in the field: anything that has sat on the ground past the delay without being collected is walked to first.
autofarm.pickup_delay.tip: How long a drop must stay uncollected before it counts as missed and gets a dedicated trip. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.auto_attack.tip: High risk: automatically attack nearby mobs once they come within reach. The default "non-violent" route turns to aim before each strike and leaves random gaps between hits, and it only turns on after you confirm the risk in a popup. May get you banned on multiplayer servers — use your own judgement.
autofarm.attack_interval.tip: Rough gap between strikes; the actual value jitters within about ±20%. Shorter looks like CPS spam and is easier to catch. Only used when "Auto-attack" is on.
autofarm.attack_target.tip: "Hostile only" attacks just hostile mobs such as zombies, skeletons and creepers. "All mobs" also includes animals and villagers. Players are never targeted.
autofarm.auto_attack_violent.tip: No turning at all: as long as the target is within attack range, strike while keeping the current view — effectively "swing and hit". The server sees a mob that is not under your crosshair losing health, which is the most anti-cheat-sensitive pattern there is. Far riskier than non-violent. Appears only after "Auto-attack" is on.
autofarm.reaction_delay.tip: Don't stop on the very same tick a threat appears (low health, hostile mobs or players nearby) — pause after a short beat instead. A human takes a few hundred milliseconds to react, and reacting faster than a machine is itself a tell. The cost is that the bot keeps working for that brief moment.
autofarm.reaction_time.tip: How long after a threat appears before it stops. Longer looks more human but leaves you exposed longer. Only used when the option above is on.
autofarm.idle_look.tip: When there's nothing to do (waiting for crops, taking a break) let the view drift slowly instead of staring at one fixed direction. It won't look around while paused for danger, and backs off the moment you move your mouse.
autofarm.option.schedule: Only work in a time window
autofarm.schedule.tip: Only harvest within the set window and stand down outside it, judged by your local time — avoiding the giveaway that "this account is online 24/7". Note: it only stops harvesting; the account stays logged in.
autofarm.schedule_start.tip: Start working at this hour each day. Click to step one hour (0-23 cycles).
autofarm.schedule_end.tip: Stop working at this hour each day (that hour excluded). Same as the start time means all day. Click to step one hour.
autofarm.notice.paused_player_near: Safety: another player is nearby, paused
autofarm.notice.paused_schedule: Extras: outside the work window, paused
